Event Description

Living cells are capable of sensing their environment, integrating this information, and making complex decisions. These decisions are, at their heart, mediated by genetically encoded molecular circuits. In the field of synthetic biology, we have been engineering modular molecular components capable of sensing and actuating and using these components to create diverse cell-based biological programs. These include programming immune cells to search the body for combinatorial molecular signatures of disease (e.g., cancer, autoimmunity, and degeneration). We are also programming multicellular systems to understand the principles that drive multi-cellular self-organization, such as the development of tissues and organs. These synthetic biology tools and approaches are helping to define the fundamental logic underlying complex biological behaviors and provide new avenues to create useful synthetic cellular devices and living materials.
